correctness.rationale: Conditional-Poisson construction proves existence and moments. The proof correctly treats the first addition output as an overdispersed Cox queue, with autocovariance s(e^{-t}+F_1(t)), and treats the shared catalyst C across the two distributed products. Independent-path product covariance, Cox superposition, two filter integrals 3/8 and 2/9, and exact variance subtraction yield the formulas for every a,b,c>0. Boundary and sign quantifiers follow because sc>0. A standalone reproducibility checker verifies 1086 rational identities/inequalities, without claiming finite tests prove the infinite-process result.

value.rationale: The 2026 source identifies mixed-operation composition as a motivated unsolved architectural direction. Exact variance at the two explicit distributive circuits, a sharp nontrivial sign change in the full three-parameter positive domain, and the stronger fourfold influence of the shared multiplier source on the sign give a concrete and operationally relevant sampling-error decision rule. It is not a mere restatement of equal means, a numerical slice, or a routine one-module variance substitution: it requires overlapping driver covariance and a second queue-filter composition.
